body:
Note for the maintainer: issue #4455 is now P1, and this PR fixes a defect that is in the v0.28.0 release.

PR #4438 (`edit_user_holder`) is in the release (the freeze notice on #681). It writes holder outlines through `HolderShape::geometry`. On a shrink-fit holder whose flange envelope covers the body, `HolderShape::of` reads back a body smaller than the real steel. An MCP edit can then write a holder outline that is smaller than the steel, and the collision checks use that outline. The GUI holder form (U12) has the same read-back.

The fix work is in progress on this PR: a merge of `main`, the MCP write through `HolderShape::component`, a refusal test for a covered body, and the targeted heavy step. The PR stays a draft until that is done. It is your decision if the cut takes it or if #4455 goes under "Known issues".

Ready for a re-check. New head: `1e899ad44`. The PR stays a draft.

What changed since `a16b70041` (the pre-review findings):

1. `git merge origin/main` (no rebase, no force-push). The merge was clean and has no hand edits. It brings in PR #4438 (`edit_user_holder`).
2. `crates/app/src/mcp/holder_shape_tools.rs`: `edit_user_holder` builds through `HolderShape::component(ADAPTIVE_PORT)`. It refuses `NotKept` with the text of the form. The tool description and `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` name the refusal.
3. `crates/app/tests/tool_library_holders/holder_shape_mcp.rs`: the fixture moves to gauge 120, where the Ø44 body shows. The shape edit goes to gauge 130 and body Ø46. A Ø48 body at gauge 130 covers the nose and is refused. The new test `mcp_edit_user_holder_refuses_a_body_the_flange_envelope_covers` pins two refusals by name, and that nothing changes:
   - an edit to a covered body;
   - an edit of a held holder with a covered body.
4. `crates/tools/src/holder_library_shape.rs`: the library shrink exception is removed. The component records no library source, and a look-alike user holder with a wider hidden body draws the same outline. A marker would change the project file, so I did not add one. Thus a covered body never reads back, also on a library copy. 44 of 117 built-in shrink chucks open in the generic editor after "Copy as user holder". The tools test pins the look-alike. The UI test now uses "BT40 Shrink 25 mm" (its body shows) and checks that a copy of "BT40 Shrink 20 mm" opens in the generic editor. The decision file records the choice and what was dropped.
5. Nits: the long doc line in `holder_form.rs` is wrapped again. The `NUDGE` comment says that the step is on a diameter and that the compare tolerance is on a radius.

Gate on `1e899ad44` (one `lanes` run): quick 182 steps 0 failed, clippy for tools, ui and app clean, light 6 steps 0 failed, and the targeted heavy step `app heavy: tool_library_holders` passes. The PR body has the details. `ready-check`: PASS.

`merge-impact`: after this PR, #4481 and #4463 conflict in `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` (a generated file: write it again). #4463 also conflicts in the `mod` list of `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests.rs`.

Quick pass: good. Head `1e899ad` merges cleanly with `main`. On this head:
- the quick gate is green (182 steps, 0 failed; it includes the tools lib, the ui lib, `tool_library_holders` and `mcp_doc_drift`);
- clippy for tools, ui and app is clean;
- the light lane is green (6 steps, 0 failed).

An independent pre-review found no blocking points. Both earlier findings are fixed. The MCP tool `edit_user_holder` writes through `HolderShape::component`, and the library shrink exception is removed. No path in this PR can write a holder outline smaller than the stated steel.

Notes for the reviewer:
- **Heavy step:** the targeted heavy step `app heavy: tool_library_holders` ran, but that binary holds 0 heavy tests. No heavy test covers `HolderShape` or `component()`, and the diff does not touch the collision, motion, simulation or post code. The real coverage is the quick plan above.
- **Screenshot:** the "after" image of the Shrink 20 copy is from an earlier head. That copy now opens in the generic component editor.
- **Older route:** the pre-review found an older route outside this diff, the gauge-length edit in the generic component editor (it finds the library body by name). It is filed as P1 #4496.

This is a P1 fix of a defect that is in the v0.28.0 release (through #4438). The maintainer merges it under the safety floor. I flag the PR ready for review.

**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.** No blockers. This is a SAFETY-tier review: holder outlines go into the collision checks.

## What looks good

- `HolderShape::of` now returns `None` when a wider body or a narrower nose draws the same outline (`crates/tools/src/holder_library_shape.rs:276-292`). A covered shrink-fit body is never read back smaller than its steel.
- `HolderShape::component` refuses a shape whose outline does not read back as the same values (`ShapeError::NotKept`). The form check, the form Apply and the MCP tool `edit_user_holder` all write through it. I found no other writer of a holder shape outline (search for `shape.geometry(` outside tests).
- The label fix is correct: the editable field is now `Body diameter`. The read-only `Largest diameter` row shows `holder_drawing::largest_d`, the same value as the drawing.
- The decision record `docs/decisions/4455-holder-largest-diameter.md` names what was dropped (the library exception, a "from the library" marker that would change the project file).
- The MCP description and `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` name the new refusal. `mcp_doc_drift` is green.
- File lengths are below 400 lines (shape 307, tests 200, form 321, MCP 135). The new test file has its provenance and gate map lines. The body has `Changelog:`, `Fixes #4455` and before/after screenshots.

## Results, merged with main (locally)

Trial merge of head `1e899ad44` with upstream/main `2394b5ad1`: clean, no conflicts. Built and tested locally on macOS (no runner).

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: **182 steps, 0 failed** (17.1 min). This includes `tools suites: lib` (239 passed), `app suites: tool_library_holders`, `app suites: mcp_doc_drift`, `app suites: example_catalog`, and `ui suites: lib`.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools|camcraft-ui|camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean (one package at a time).

Extra suites run: none owed. The diff changes no `testdata/` file and no importer code. No recorded program (`*.nc`, `*.cl`, `examples/catalog/**`) changed.

Heavy lanes: not run. No collaborator heavy record names this head. The author ran `app heavy: tool_library_holders` (0 ignored tests in that binary). Heavy lanes are not a merge condition.

## Mutations (safety tier)

1. `of` returns the first match without the covered-body check (`return Some(s)`): **red**. `a_body_the_flange_envelope_covers_is_not_read_back_smaller`, `an_edited_outline_is_never_smaller_than_the_steel` and `each_builtin_taper_holder_reads_back_as_its_shape` fail.
2. `edit_user_holder` builds with `kind()` + `geometry()` and not through `component()`: **red**. `mcp_edit_user_holder_refuses_a_body_the_flange_envelope_covers` fails.

The source was restored after each mutation. Nothing was pushed.

## Requested before merge

None.

## Optional, non-blocking (follow-ups, P7)

1. The MCP argument `largest_d` of `edit_user_holder` now has the meaning of the form field `Body diameter`. The form uses `Largest diameter` for the outline value. An agent can read the two names as one value. Suggest an alias `body_d`, or a description line that says `largest_d` is the body steel.
2. `ShapeError::NotKept` always says that the flange envelope covers the body. `of` also refuses a shape when a narrower nose draws the same outline. In that case the text names the wrong cause. Suggest a second variant or a more general text.
3. A user holder with a covered body that a project file holds from before this fix now opens in the generic component editor. The body says so under "Not exercised". A test that opens such a project is not in the PR.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
